newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX ends above 2,800 pts, but off day high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX ends above 2,800 pts, but off day high.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares ended bourse dealings above the magical 2,800 point level for the first time ever on Tuesday, spurred on by another record on Wall Street overnight and a firmer dollar.
The DAX index ended up 11.45 points, or 0.41 percent, at 2,810.64 points, earlier touching a bourse record high of 2,819.95 points, before slipping back slightly on profit-taking.

The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day trade in the DAX index, ended at 2,808.62, paring about ten points in late dealings as the dollar came off the day's highs and Wall Street reversed early gains and fell into negative territory.
Dealers said the directon of the dollar would continue to provide direction for the market this week.
"Everyone just keeps buying. We're seeing an across-the-board rally," said one trader.

Dealers said the stronger dollar, which pulled above the 1.52 mark level late on Monday and continued to climb on Tuesday, was helping the chemical and auto sectors in particular, both of which are export-oriented and benefit from a weaker mark.
On Tuesday afternoon, the dollar attempted to breach the 1.53 mark level, before falling back under 1.525 marks.

In the car sector, BMW and Daimler-Benz AG stocks both charged ahead to new record highs. BMW shares hit a year high of 995.25, before profit-taking brought the stock back to end computer trade 981.10 marks, still up 15.60 marks.
Daimler shares reached an all-time high of 100.75 marks in IBIS dealings, but then pared gains to end up 50 pfennigs at 99.75 marks.
Amongst the chemical companies, BASF AG, Hoechst AG and Bayer AG all reached new year highs, encouraging the rest of the market.

Meanwhile, shares in troubled construction firm Philipp Holzmann took a tumble, falling 19 marks, or almost five percent, to 367 marks, after Deutsche Morgan Grenfell raised its loss forecast for the firm.
Dealers said they saw the current rally continuing until at least the end of the year, with 2,850 points the next major technical resistance level for the DAX to test.
But they said volumes could trail off at the end of the week, with the Thanksgiving public holiday in the U.S on Thursday.
